jobs.description:
Job Summary

The Assistant Director of Development for Health & Sciences Development & Alumni Relations is an experienced professional who has the ability to practice, and/or has knowledge of, the fundraising field, with the ability to apply fundraising theory to the full range of responsibilities of a university development officer. This position analyzes problems/issues of varied scope, and determines solutions, and plans, schedules, and implements comprehensive fundraising projects and programs, including fundraising programs such as the Children’s Miracle Network.

This position is metric-driven and expected to raise gift dollar amounts as established through an annual business planning process and aligned with the assigned portfolio. This is a fundraising position focused on developing new and fostering established donor relationships. Guided by a “donor centric” approach, the incumbent will strategically solicit gifts and steward existing ones using various communication methods, including in person, video, texting, phone, social media and virtual visits. This position requires good judgment in selecting methods and techniques for obtaining solutions, and works independently, collaboratively, and collegially as part of a large, matrix organization.

September 10, 2026 at 11:59pm.

Initial Application Review date is August 26, 2026. Interviews and recruiting process may occur at any time. Position will remain open until filled.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s Degree or equivalent education and experience.
Experience demonstrated through 1 or more years of professional or volunteer fundraising experience; or equivalent transferrable professional experience including strategic relationship development and portfolio management; or equivalent combination of experience and education.
Strong written, oral and interpersonal communication skills to establish and maintain good working relationships at all organizational levels and with outside constituencies, including donors and volunteers, to develop collaborative working relationships needed to accomplish organizational goals.

Preferred Qualifications

Awareness, knowledge, and skill in applying inclusion to one’s work. A profound belief in the value of a safe workforce and a commitment to achieve this goal through collaboration and team building, working cooperatively with a large group of department and campus constituencies.
Demonstrated experience in developing strategic relationships with businesses, corporations, individual donors and prospective donors, foundations, and other philanthropic organizations and researching, building and managing a portfolio of donors and prospects with a goal of raising philanthropic funds.

20% - Development Operations

Development & Alumni Relations (DEVAR) provides leadership in building enduring public trust, understanding, and support for UC Davis and its mission of teaching, research, and public service. DEVAR provides leadership, coordination and support services to help the university meet its mission of research, teaching and service by building philanthropic support and executing approved fundraising programs that support the university's highest priorities and initiatives.

Description

At Northrop Grumman, our employees have incredible opportunities to work on revolutionary systems that impact people's lives around the world today, and for generations to come. Our pioneering and inventive spirit has enabled us to be at the forefront of many technological advancements in our nation's history - from the first flight across the Atlantic Ocean, to stealth bombers, to landing on the moon. We look for people who have bold new ideas, courage and a pioneering spirit to join forces to invent the future, and have fun along the way. Our culture thrives on intellectual curiosity, cognitive diversity and bringing your whole self to work — and we have an insatiable drive to do what others think is impossible. Our employees are not only part of history, they're making history.

Northrop Grumman’s Defense Systems Sector
is looking for a Missile Production Program Director
for our advanced missile programs within the Air Warfare Systems (AWS) Operating Unit, located in the heart of Northridge, CA
.

This is a rare opportunity to lead at the intersection of advanced weapons, digital manufacturing, and national security—where disciplined execution and modern production approaches directly enable mission success.

This role sits at the cornerstone of Northrop Grumman’s advanced weapons product lines, shaping how next-generation missile capabilities transition from development into scalable, rate production. The production systems, factories, and supplier partnerships you build will directly influence the affordability, availability, and readiness of critical missile capabilities for the U.S. Department of Defense and allied partners.

This position is required to be full-time, on-site in the Northridge, CA location. No remote/telework arrangement is available for this position. Applicants must have an active US Government DoD Secret security clearance with ability to get cleared for SAP
.

We are intentionally seeking leaders who bring fresh perspective and proven execution strength, including those from non-traditional but highly relevant industries such as advanced manufacturing, automotive, space, industrial automation, and high-reliability technology environments. If you have led complex products from prototype to scaled production—and are energized by applying modern manufacturing and digital tools to mission-critical systems—this role offers a unique and meaningful challenge.

As Program Director of production, you will lead the transition from development to production, guide production start-up, and scale execution across a portfolio of advanced missile programs. You will be responsible for establishing production excellence as a strategic advantage—leveraging automation, digital transformation, advanced analytics, and emerging machine learning capabilities to deliver speed, quality, and affordability at scale.

Reporting directly to the AWS Operating Unit Director, you will be a key member of the senior leadership team, executing an ambitious strategic plan supported by significant technology, capital, and workforce investments.

Key Responsibilities

Own end-to-end production execution for advanced missile programs, from late-stage development and transition to production through start-up, ramp, and sustained-rate delivery
Provide full P&L leadership across multiple production programs, ensuring cost, schedule, quality, and performance commitments are met or exceeded
Lead industrialization and scale-up efforts for cornerstone advanced weapons product lines, including factory readiness, capacity planning, workforce growth, and capital deployment
Drive automation and digital manufacturing transformation, applying digital thread concepts, advanced analytics, and machine learning to improve throughput, predictability, and quality
Build resilient supplier and industrial base partnerships, collaborating across the value chain to ensure capacity, affordability, and long-term sustainability for missile production
Lead and develop high-performing, multidisciplinary teams, fostering a culture of ownership, accountability, and continuous improvement
Navigate and resolve complex technical, manufacturing, and supply chain challenges inherent to advanced missile production with speed, clarity, and disciplined execution
Partner seamlessly across engineering, quality, supply chain, finance, contracts, and program management to deliver integrated, executable production strategies
Execute disciplined risk and opportunity management, proactively mitigating production risk while capturing productivity and cost-reduction opportunities
Support capture and proposal activities, shaping production strategies, schedules, and cost positions that strengthen competitive posture
Communicate with confidence and transparency to customers, senior leadership, and enterprise stakeholders
Ensure compliance with contract requirements, internal processes, and applicable regulatory and industry standards

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree with 10 years of experience in production, operations, manufacturing, and program execution; or Master’s degree with 8 years of the same experience mentioned
5 years of experience leading high performing, production or operational, cross-functional teams within the aerospace/defense sector with accountability for cost, schedule, and quality
Experience in successfully transitioning advanced products from development or pilot phases into scaled production with ability to manage revenue, profit, and cash performance
Experience in managing and partnering with suppliers and industrial partners
Strong judgment and decision-making skills that balance execution urgency with long-term business outcomes
Active US Government DoD Secret security clearance with ability to get cleared for SAP

Preferred Qualifications

Active Top Secret clearance (or prior experience working in cleared or highly regulated environments)
Experience as a Prime Contractor or as a production leader in high-reliability, high-consequence industries (missiles, aerospace, automotive, space, industrial automation)
Demonstrated leadership in automation, digital manufacturing, advanced analytics, or AI/ML-enabled production systems
Experience leading production start-ups, factory launches, or major rate increases
Proven adaptability—successfully bringing modern production practices into complex, mission-driven environments while maintaining strong stakeholder relationships

Living in Northridge offers a perfect combination of urban living with the beauty of nature. It is a short drive away from downtown Los Angeles, the Hollywood Hills, or the rest of the San Fernando Valley. Take advantage of your flexible work schedule to enjoy shopping at the local Northridge Fashion Center or spend time at the local Recreation Center as well as easy access to nearby protected natural areas such as the Chatsworth Reservoir, the Santa Susana Pass State Historic Park, Lake Balboa or within driving distance, spend a day at the beach. jobs.description:
Build Our Future Together

At Regeneron, we use science and innovation to develop life-changing medicines for people with serious diseases. We are seeking an Executive Director
to join our Patient Safety
team.

The Executive Director, Global Patient Safety Sciences Delivery serves as the key point of contact for all Safety Sciences operations and risk-related responsibilities across all Therapeutic Areas (TAs). This role is responsible for driving consistency across the portfolio for standard activities performed by the Safety Scientists (e.g., data transformation, safety surveillance, SMT preparation, early draft of aggregate reports, signal evaluations, label enhancement justifications). This role is also responsible for the processes and written procedures that underpin the safety governance, and other fundamental processes within Safety Sciences. This role requires the ability to work cross-functionally, partnering with the Safety Sciences TAHs and other leaders. They will serve as a member of the GPS Leadership Team (GPS LT). The Executive Director, Global Patient Safety Sciences Delivery is also responsible for the development and management of their team.

This position offers the opportunity to contribute to a fast-growing, science-driven organization making a meaningful difference to patients worldwide.

When & Where

Work Location: Tarrytown, NY, Warren, NJ or Cambridge, MA
Hybrid: 4 days per week onsite
Travel: As needed

Discover Your Role

Define the strategy to ensure standardization and consistency in execution of core activities (e.g., signal detection, authoring sections for safety documents) across all products and TAs through development of common practices, processes, templates
Oversee relevant training programs for GPS Safety Sciences, including a standardized training curriculum, proficiency matrix, and knowledge management repository
Enable the Global Capability Center (GCC) to operate more efficiency and scale with the demands of the business
Develop innovative approaches to delivering on core activities that integrate in new technologies, including AI

Operational Delivery Oversight

Ensure compliance and quality management of Safety Sciences Operations activities, including compliance with all regulations and establishment of SOPs and associated monitoring tools
Oversee all aspects of signal detection coordination and signal management process across all TAs, including Safety Monitoring Team (SMT), Safety Surveillance Plan (SSP) and Signal Evaluation Report (SER)
Coordinate and support high quality, timely, and compliant delivery of benefit-risk assessment for periodic safety reports (e.g., DSURs, PSURs) and support Safety Sciences Strategy in contributing Medical and Safety perspective to the GPS portfolio of documents (e.g., ARM, RMP, SMP) where required
Set and oversee the framework for aggregate safety data analysis to ensure effective coordination and delivery

Cross-Functional Partnership

Serve as strategic point of contact to enable SS operational delivery in partnership with TAHs and GPS Leads
Partner with key Regeneron interfaces (e.g., Clinical, Regulatory, Med Affairs, Biostats & Data Management)

Talent Development & Organizational Leadership

Build, coach, and scale a high-performing team, and drive succession planning and talent pipelines
Lead talent strategy and leadership development initiatives that strengthen capabilities across the organization.

This Role Requires

Minimum M.D., PA, PhD or PharmD Degree; Board Certification or equivalent in relevant clinical specialty, MBA is an advantage.
17+ years total experience in PV or relevant clinical experience in the pharmaceutical industry required
6+ years of leading a team and people management experience
Preferred experience with oversight of operations within a global patient safety organization
Strong attention to detail with the ability to assess and optimize Safety operations processes, drive consistency, and ensure high-quality, compliant execution across activities
Strong leadership capabilities and presence, interpersonal, verbal and written communication skills organizational and workload planning skills along with the ability to manage multiple different projects simultaneously

About The Role

As the Executive Director
, you will oversee all strategic, financial, and operational aspects of the ProAmpac Employee Assistance Fund (PEAF). You will carry out the vision of the organization, leading efforts to scale the fund globally, engage our workforce, and ensure the fund's long-term sustainability.

Whether you are navigating compliance, collaborating with the Board of Directors, or visiting our manufacturing sites to raise awareness, your leadership will directly support employees when they need it most.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership & Global Expansion
Drive Vision: Provide overall leadership and direction for the PEAF, aligning the program with ProAmpac's core values: Integrity, Intensity, Innovation, Involvement, and Impact.
Expand Our Reach: Lead the expansion of the fund to international locations and newly acquired manufacturing sites, adapting processes to respect regional HR policies and practices.
Growth Strategy: Develop and execute strategic plans to scale program participation, overall funding, and community impact.
Program Administration & Compliance
Daily Operations: Oversee the day-to-day administration of the grant process, ensuring applications are handled fairly, efficiently, and with the strictest confidentiality.
Regulatory Compliance: Maintain rigorous records of all grants, donor contributions, and fund activities. Ensure full compliance with nonprofit governance, tax regulations, and legal guidelines.
Digital Resources: Manage the PEAF website and promotional materials to ensure easy, seamless access to applications and contribution portals.
Board Governance & Financial Sustainability
Board Collaboration: Partner closely with the Board of Directors to guide policy development, long-term planning, and strategic decisions.
Reporting: Prepare and deliver program metrics, financial updates, and impact reports for board meetings.
Fundraising: Design and champion creative fundraising initiatives, including annual donor campaigns, employee payroll deduction programs, and special events.
Employee Engagement & Advocacy
Raise Awareness: Partner with HR and plant managers to educate our workforce on how to contribute to the fund and how to apply for support.
In-Person Outreach: Conduct site visits, deliver presentations, and host employee meetings to build trust and drive engagement across all locations.

Qualifications & Experience

What You Bring to the Team

You should be fastidious about excellence, extremely organized, attentive to detail, and motivated by the service function itself. You communicate clearly and effectively in writing and in person and handle sensitive information with absolute discretion. You are energized by the dynamic nature of the role.

This is not a role for someone who needs a rigid operating system, a predictable workday, or a principal whose working style always follows a set process. Northrop Grumman’s Defense Systems Sector
is looking for a Missile Production Program Director
for our advanced missile programs within the Air Warfare Systems (AWS) Operating Unit, located in the heart of Northridge, CA
.

This is a rare opportunity to lead at the intersection of advanced weapons, digital manufacturing, and national security—where disciplined execution and modern production approaches directly enable mission success.

This role sits at the cornerstone of Northrop Grumman’s advanced weapons product lines, shaping how next-generation missile capabilities transition from development into scalable, rate production. The production systems, factories, and supplier partnerships you build will directly influence the affordability, availability, and readiness of critical missile capabilities for the U.S. Department of Defense and allied partners.

This position is required to be full-time, on-site in the Northridge, CA location. No remote/telework arrangement is available for this position. Applicants must have an active US Government DoD Secret security clearance with ability to get cleared for SAP
.

We are intentionally seeking leaders who bring fresh perspective and proven execution strength, including those from non-traditional but highly relevant industries such as advanced manufacturing, automotive, space, industrial automation, and high-reliability technology environments. If you have led complex products from prototype to scaled production—and are energized by applying modern manufacturing and digital tools to mission-critical systems—this role offers a unique and meaningful challenge.

As Program Director of production, you will lead the transition from development to production, guide production start-up, and scale execution across a portfolio of advanced missile programs. You will be responsible for establishing production excellence as a strategic advantage—leveraging automation, digital transformation, advanced analytics, and emerging machine learning capabilities to deliver speed, quality, and affordability at scale.

Reporting directly to the AWS Operating Unit Director, you will be a key member of the senior leadership team, executing an ambitious strategic plan supported by significant technology, capital, and workforce investments.

Key Responsibilities

Own end-to-end production execution for advanced missile programs, from late-stage development and transition to production through start-up, ramp, and sustained-rate delivery
Provide full P&L leadership across multiple production programs, ensuring cost, schedule, quality, and performance commitments are met or exceeded
Lead industrialization and scale-up efforts for cornerstone advanced weapons product lines, including factory readiness, capacity planning, workforce growth, and capital deployment
Drive automation and digital manufacturing transformation, applying digital thread concepts, advanced analytics, and machine learning to improve throughput, predictability, and quality
Build resilient supplier and industrial base partnerships, collaborating across the value chain to ensure capacity, affordability, and long-term sustainability for missile production
Lead and develop high-performing, multidisciplinary teams, fostering a culture of ownership, accountability, and continuous improvement
Navigate and resolve complex technical, manufacturing, and supply chain challenges inherent to advanced missile production with speed, clarity, and disciplined execution
Partner seamlessly across engineering, quality, supply chain, finance, contracts, and program management to deliver integrated, executable production strategies
Execute disciplined risk and opportunity management, proactively mitigating production risk while capturing productivity and cost-reduction opportunities
Support capture and proposal activities, shaping production strategies, schedules, and cost positions that strengthen competitive posture
Communicate with confidence and transparency to customers, senior leadership, and enterprise stakeholders
Ensure compliance with contract requirements, internal processes, and applicable regulatory and industry standards

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree with 10 years of experience in production, operations, manufacturing, and program execution; or Master’s degree with 8 years of the same experience mentioned
5 years of experience leading high performing, production or operational, cross-functional teams within the aerospace/defense sector with accountability for cost, schedule, and quality
Experience in successfully transitioning advanced products from development or pilot phases into scaled production with ability to manage revenue, profit, and cash performance
Experience in managing and partnering with suppliers and industrial partners
Strong judgment and decision-making skills that balance execution urgency with long-term business outcomes
Active US Government DoD Secret security clearance with ability to get cleared for SAP

Preferred Qualifications

Active Top Secret clearance (or prior experience working in cleared or highly regulated environments)
Experience as a Prime Contractor or as a production leader in high-reliability, high-consequence industries (missiles, aerospace, automotive, space, industrial automation)
Demonstrated leadership in automation, digital manufacturing, advanced analytics, or AI/ML-enabled production systems
Experience leading production start-ups, factory launches, or major rate increases

About The Company

We are a renewable energy and ocean technology company committed to rapidly developing and deploying technologies that will ensure a sustainable future for Earth by unlocking the vast energy potential of its oceans. Our focus is on capturing civilizational levels of ultra-low-cost renewable energy for applications including computing and affordable renewable fuels delivered to shore.

The company is a public benefit corporation headquartered in Portland, Oregon, and backed by leading venture capitalists, philanthropic investors, university endowments, and private investment offices. We operate as an idea meritocracy in which the best ideas change the company’s direction on a regular basis.

About The Job

This role provides direct support to a fast-moving CEO, designing and administering the core systems that keep his world running smoothly in a rapidly changing environment. This is a hands-on, high-trust role. Your job is to ensure nothing gets dropped and that the CEO is responsive, on time and prepared, and free to focus on the highest-leverage work.

This is a no-task-too-small role that requires sound judgment at every level. You work closely with the Chief of Staff to the CEO and own the CEO’s day-to-day, including inbox, calendar, travel, coordination, events, and external engagements, while also managing personal logistics to make his life run more efficiently.

The work requires speed, discretion, strong writing, practical problem-solving, and context switching between professional and personal support throughout the day. You should be equally enthusiastic about coordinating a board meeting and picking up dry cleaning.

You should be fastidious about excellence, extremely organized, attentive to detail, and motivated by the service function itself. You have low ego, strong follow-through, high personal energy, and the ability to be warm and good-humored while maintaining polish. You communicate clearly and effectively in writing and in person and handle sensitive information with absolute discretion. You are energized by the dynamic nature of the role.

This is not a role for someone who needs a rigid operating system, a predictable workday, or a principal whose working style always follows a set process. This role requires a great degree of flexibility, and in return offers unusually valuable experience for someone wanting to sharpen their judgment in a high-dimensional environment while making a large impact.

Responsibilities

Inbox & Communications: Manage the CEO’s inbox and inbound communications with exceptional responsiveness. Raise urgent items, draft crisp, clear, tactful communications, and develop and send predetermined responses as appropriate.
Calendar & Scheduling: Own the CEO’s calendar and scheduling including prioritization, protecting focus time, and optimizing for efficiency and daily flow. Coordinate effectively with internal and external stakeholders cleanly and without creating friction. Support scheduling for other company leaders at the CEO’s discretion.
Event & Visit Coordination: Own planning, coordination, and execution for site visits and external engagement including investor visits, group tours, speaking opportunities, and media appearances.
Travel: Arrange CEO travel including last-minute bookings, transportation, required documentation, and occasional on-the-ground support. Support travel arrangements for other company leaders at the CEO’s discretion.
Meeting Preparation & Follow-Through: Ensure the CEO is on time and prepared for meetings and commitments by managing reminders and the capturing of key details such as important decisions, follow-ups, and next steps.
Confidentiality & Judgment: Handle sensitive personal and professional information with absolute discretion. Read situations well, including when to engage, when to be brief, and when not to interrupt.
Personal Assistance & Life Infrastructure: Help make the CEO’s life easier in practical, concrete ways by noticing and addressing needs and reducing recurring sources of friction. Build and maintain low-touch, reliable systems for facilitating household management, appointments, errands, and other personal logistics.

Required Qualifications

This is not a 9-to-5 role; you should be willing to monitor and respond to time-sensitive communications across a wide daily window, including evenings and weekends
Proven professional experience in a role requiring exceptional organization, judgment, discretion, and coordination of complex priorities in a fast-paced environment
Fast response times and reliable follow-through, with the ability to move quickly on email, scheduling, travel, and logistics without becoming frantic or careless
Experience partnering with executives and senior leaders, coordinating seamlessly across multiple stakeholders, driving complex priorities to completion while building trust and maintaining strong relationships
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to represent executives and the company with professionalism and discretion
Fast and accurate typing skills to support rapid drafting, note-taking, and communication
Exceptional organization and attention to detail, with a proven track record of managing multiple complex workstreams simultaneously
Strong relationship memory and social awareness, including tracking names, organizations, prior interactions, relevant context, and connections across a broad network
Strong computer proficiency and demonstrated skill in quickly learning and adapting to new software, systems, and digital tools; familiarity with Google Workspace, Slack, spreadsheets and relational databases, and comparable platforms
Demonstrated ability to operate effectively amid ambiguity and rapid change in a low-control environment, with comfort context switching throughout the day
A grounded demeanor under pressure, and a consistent ability to create and maintain a low-friction working environment
A service-oriented, no-task-too-small mindset and willingness to handle both strategic responsibilities and day-to-day operational functions with equal care
High personal energy, tact, warmth, and good humor
Strong interpersonal instincts, sound situational awareness, and a track record of building trust in relationships
Absolute discretion with sensitive personal, professional, and company information
Willingness to seek, receive, and incorporate direct feedback as part of Panthalassa’s high-trust, high-performance culture

Desired Qualifications

Experience in an executive assistant, personal assistant, or founder support role
Strong travel-planning experience, including complex itineraries and frequent changes
Familiarity with AI tools and comfort using them to improve speed, organization, research, drafting, scheduling, and day-to-day workflows
Curiosity and judgment about where automation can reduce friction without compromising quality, discretion, or accuracy
Track record of actively seeking and incorporating feedback

Strong candidates may come from a range of backgrounds. We encourage you to apply if you are a strong candidate with only some of the desired skills and experience listed.

Additional Requirements

Must be based in or near Portland, Oregon, or willing to relocate rapidly (relocation assistance provided)
Must have a valid driver’s license

Compensation And Benefits

If hired for this full-time role, you will receive:

Cash compensation of $130,000–$195,000.
Equity in the company. We’re all owners and if we’re successful, this equity should be far and away the most valuable component of your compensation.
A benefits package that helps you take care of yourself and your family, including:

Health insurance (the company pays 100% of gold level PPO plan for full time employees, their partners, and dependents)

Disability insurance (the company pays 100% for a policy to provide long term financial support if you become disabled)
Ability to contribute to tax-advantaged accounts, including 401(k), health FSA, and dependent care FSA

Relocation assistance to facilitate your move to Portland (if needed).
